Put \(L^{0,(a)}=I_p-B^{0,(a)}\) and \(\mathcal L^0=\operatorname{diag}_{a\in M}(L^{0,(a)})\).  By \(\texttt{ass:shared-topological-order}\), every \(L^{0,(a)}\), and hence \(\mathcal L^0\), is invertible.  If \(\Omega\) is the covariance of the view-stacked disturbance vector, then \(\texttt{ass:component-aligned-disturbances}\) gives
\[
 \Omega[(a,i),(b,j)]={\bf1}\{i=j\}\Gamma_i[a,b].
 \tag{1}
\]
After grouping indices by \(i\), (1) is \(\operatorname{diag}_{i\in V}(\Gamma_i)\succ0\) by \(\texttt{ass:disturbance-positive-definiteness}\).  The structural equations therefore give
\[
 \Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}
 = (\mathcal L^0)^{-1}\Omega(\mathcal L^0)^{-\mathsf T}\succ0.
 \tag{2}
\]
Thus every \(\Sigma^{aa}\), every principal matrix \(\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]\), and every within-view Schur complement \(C_A^{aa}\) is positive definite.  In particular all inverses in the definitions exist and \(C_A^{aa}[r,r]>0\).

Fix \(A\subseteq V\), \(r\in U_A\), and \(t\in U_A\setminus\{r\}\).  Successive least-squares projection first on \(X_A^{(b)}\) and then on the residual of \(X_r^{(b)}\) is the unique projection on \(X_{A\cup\{r\}}^{(b)}\).  Hence
\[
 Z_{A\cup\{r\},t}^{(b)}
 =Z_{A,t}^{(b)}-
 \frac{C_A^{bb}[t,r]}{C_A^{bb}[r,r]}Z_{A,r}^{(b)}.
\]
Taking covariance with \(Z_{A,r}^{(a)}\), using symmetry of \(C_A^{bb}\), and applying \(\texttt{def:q-root-score}\) yields
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_P(Z_{A,r}^{(a)},Z_{A\cup\{r\},t}^{(b)})
 =q^{ab}(A,r,t).
 \tag{3}
\]
This also proves that the recursively obtained residual state is the path-independent state of \(\texttt{def:projected-residual-state}\).

Fix an order of \(W=U_A\setminus\{r\}\).  Sequential within-view regression in view \(b\) supplies an invertible unit triangular residualizer \(K^{(b)}\) with \(e_W^{(b)}=K^{(b)}Z_{A\cup\{r\},W}^{(b)}\), while \(e_r^{(a)}=Z_{A,r}^{(a)}\).  Equation (3), coordinate by coordinate, gives
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_P(e_r^{(a)},e_W^{(b)})
 =\bigl(q^{ab}(A,r,t):t\in W\bigr)(K^{(b)})^{\mathsf T}.
 \tag{4}
\]
Invertibility of \(K^{(b)}\) makes the left side zero exactly when every score on the right is zero.  Exchanging \(a\) and \(b\) supplies the tail-to-root column criterion.  Induction over successive roots, with the one-coordinate suffix as the vacuous base case, proves
\[
 \pi\text{ is a source-to-sink path in }\mathcal D_G
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \operatorname{offdiag}(R_\pi^{ab})=0
 \text{ for every }\{a,b\}\in E.
 \tag{5}
\]
The within-view normal equations separately imply that every \(R_\pi^{aa}\) is diagonal with positive diagonal.

For any candidate \(\pi\), put
\[
 \mathcal L_\pi=\operatorname{diag}_{a\in M}(L_\pi^{(a)}),
 \qquad S_\pi=\mathcal L_\pi\Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}
 \mathcal L_\pi^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Equation (2) and invertibility of \(\mathcal L_\pi\) imply \(S_\pi\succ0\).  Let \(H_{\pi,j}\) be its principal submatrix on \(\{(a,j):a\in M\}\).  Extending a nonzero vector by zeros proves \(H_{\pi,j}\succ0\).  On every observed block,
\[
 S_\pi^{ab}=L_\pi^{(a)}\Sigma^{ab}(L_\pi^{(b)})^{\mathsf T}=R_\pi^{ab},
\]
so \(H_{\pi,j}\) completes \(Q_{\pi,j}\).

Suppose first that \(\pi\) is a path.  By (5), the observed edge blocks \(R_\pi^{ab}\) are diagonal.  Independently for each \(j\), choose a centered Gaussian vector \((\eta_j^{(a)})_{a\in M}\) with covariance \(H_{\pi,j}\), and make these vectors independent across \(j\).  Set \(\eta^{(a)}=(\eta_j^{(a)}:j\in V)\) and \(\widetilde X^{(a)}=(L_\pi^{(a)})^{-1}\eta^{(a)}\).  The resulting disturbance coordinates are independent within each view, component aligned across views, and have positive-definite coordinate covariance blocks \(H_{\pi,j}\).  Moreover, for \(a=b\) or \(\{a,b\}\in E\), diagonality and the completion identities give
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(\widetilde X^{(a)},\widetilde X^{(b)})
 =(L_\pi^{(a)})^{-1}R_\pi^{ab}(L_\pi^{(b)})^{-\mathsf T}
 =\Sigma^{ab}.
 \tag{6}
\]
Thus the constructed Gaussian mechanism belongs to \(\mathfrak F_G^{\mathrm{CA}}(\mathcal O_G)\), has order \(\pi\), and has coefficient tuple \(T_\pi\).  By \(\texttt{def:compatible-orders}\), \(\pi\in\Pi_G^{\mathrm{CA}}(\mathcal O_G)\).

Conversely, let \(\pi\in\Pi_G^{\mathrm{CA}}(\mathcal O_G)\) and take a witnessing mechanism in \(\mathfrak F_G^{\mathrm{CA}}(\mathcal O_G)\).  Because \(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{CA}}\subseteq\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{pub}}\), this witness lies in \(\mathfrak F_G(\mathcal O_G)\).  The converse normal-equation part of \(\texttt{thm:published-all-orders-covariance-compatible}\) forces its coefficient family to be \(B_\pi\).  Its observed residual blocks are consequently \(R_\pi^{ab}\).  Component alignment makes their off-diagonal coordinate entries zero, and the witnessing matrices \(\widetilde\Gamma_j\succ0\) complete the corresponding \(Q_{\pi,j}\).  Equation (5) now makes \(\pi\) a source-to-sink path.  This proves the equivalence, the stated principal-block completions, and the independent Gaussian completion claim.

Let \(\mathcal P_A\) be the set of full-lattice prefixes from \(\varnothing\) to \(A\).  Induction on \(|A|\), using \(\texttt{def:fragment-hashcons-enumerator}\), gives
\[
 H_A=\{F(\rho):\rho\in\mathcal P_A\}.
 \tag{10}
\]
The initialization proves (10) for \(A=\varnothing\).  Every nonempty prefix to \(A'\) has a final edge \(A'\setminus\{r\}\to A'\); by induction its parent fragment is present, and the transition writes exactly \(\beta(A'\setminus\{r\},r)\).  Conversely, every insertion extends a represented prefix by one full-lattice edge.  Exact trie equality removes precisely duplicate fragments.

Fix \(F\in H_A\) and a representing prefix \(\rho\).  Choose any suffix.  The resulting permutation belongs to \(\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)\) by \(\texttt{thm:published-all-orders-covariance-compatible}\), so its tuple lies in \(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\).  By \(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\), every \(T\in\operatorname{Comp}(\rho)\) satisfies
\[
 T\big|_{\text{rows indexed by }A}=F.
 \tag{11}
\]
The nonempty completion sets for unequal fragments are disjoint by \(\texttt{lem:live-fragment-right-congruence}\) and are subsets of \(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\).  Hence
\[
 |H_A|\le|\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)|=N_{\mathrm{out}}.
 \tag{12}
\]
Summing (12) over all \(2^p\) subsets gives \(\sum_A|H_A|\le2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}\).  Since each retained fragment is processed once and each subset has at most \(p\) outgoing edges,
\[
 \sum_{A\subseteq V}(p-|A|)|H_A|
 \le p\sum_{A\subseteq V}|H_A|
 \le p2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}.
\]

Induction on \(|A|\), exactly as in (10), proves that \(H_A\) contains precisely the distinct fragments of full-lattice prefixes ending at \(A\).  Merging equal fragments preserves every continuation by \(\texttt{lem:live-fragment-right-congruence}\).  At \(A=V\), every row is assigned, and \(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\) identifies the decoded fragment of an order \(\pi\) with \(T_\pi\).  The two directions of \(\texttt{thm:published-all-orders-covariance-compatible}\), together with the mechanism-projection definition \(\texttt{def:identified-tuple-set}\), therefore give
\[
 \{\text{decoded members of }H_V\}
 =\{T_\pi:\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\}
 =\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G).
 \tag{13}
\]
For each original row label, lexicographic exact-real sorting assigns one integer identifier exactly to numerically equal viewwise rows.  Trie insertion creates a terminal only on the first occurrence of an integer fragment.  Equation (13) is therefore emitted without omission and exactly once per numerical tuple.

We count ordered exact-real operations.  The full lattice has \(2^p\) vertices and \(p2^{p-1}\) edges; its vacuous forward-backward pruning costs \(O(p2^p)\).  For fixed \(A\) and view \(a\), one dense factorization of \(\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]\), followed by all solves for \(r\notin A\), computes the outgoing rows in \(O(p^3)\) operations.  These matrices are invertible by \(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\), so all rows cost
\[
 O(mp^3 2^p).
 \tag{14}
\]
For fixed row label \(r\), at most \(K_r=2^{p-1}\) edges carry that label.  A lexicographic comparison examines at most \(mp\) real coordinates.  Comparison sorting and adjacent equality interning cost
\[
 O\!\left(mp\sum_{r\in V}K_r\log(K_r+1)\right)
 =O(mp^3 2^p).
 \tag{15}
\]
No real-valued hash is used.  A row identifier has \(O(p)\) bits and a fragment has \(p\) slots, so deterministic binary-trie lookup or insertion costs \(O(p^2)\).  By \(\texttt{lem:projection-output-bound}\), at most \(p2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}\) transitions are attempted, and propagation therefore costs
\[
 O(p^3 2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}).
 \tag{16}
\]
Decoding and emitting \(m\) matrices with \(p^2\) entries costs \(O(mp^2N_{\mathrm{out}})\).

By \(\texttt{prop:published-common-union-support-ancestry-empty}\), published-class common ancestry is always the empty relation.  It is returned in \(O(1)\) time and space and requires no output scan.  Adding (14)--(16) yields the displayed time bound.

For space, the interned rows occupy \(O(mp^2 2^p)\) real cells, the tries occupy \(O(p^2 2^pN_{\mathrm{out}})\) bits or pointers by the projection bound, decoded retained outputs occupy \(O(mp^2N_{\mathrm{out}})\) cells, and the lattice costs \(O(p2^p)\).  The published output is nonempty by \(\texttt{thm:published-all-orders-covariance-compatible}\).  Both total time and space are consequently \(O(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p\max\{1,N_{\mathrm{out}}\})\).  Every loop ranges over subset edges and retained fragments, never over \(p!\) permutations, and no cross-view residual zero is used to screen a published-class order.

Assume \(B^{0,(a)}=0\) for every \(a\in M\).  By \(\texttt{ass:linear-structural-equations}\), \(X^{(a)}=\varepsilon^{(a)}\).  The within-view product condition in \(\texttt{ass:centered-gaussian-law}\) and the positive-variance clause in \(\texttt{def:published-limvam-class}\) give a positive diagonal matrix \(\Sigma^{aa}\).  Thus, for every \(A\subseteq V\) and \(r\notin A\),
\[
 \Sigma^{aa}[r,A]=0,
 \qquad \beta^{(a)}(A,r)=0.
 \tag{17}
\]
By \(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\), every order induces the all-zero tuple.  By \(\texttt{thm:published-all-orders-covariance-compatible}\), every one of the \(p!\) orders is compatible for every \(G\), hence for the empty graph, and
\[
 \Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)=\{0\},
 \qquad N_{\mathrm{out}}=1.
\]
Starting from the unique empty fragment, every transition writes a zero row by (17).  Exact trie insertion retains the resulting identical fragment once in each subset bucket.  There are \(2^p\) buckets, proving the claim.

Write every rational input coordinate in lowest terms with positive denominator.  For one principal regression solve, multiply its coefficient matrix and right-hand side by the product \(d\) of the denominators of the at most \((p+1)^2\) entries in the augmented matrix.  If each numerator and denominator has at most \(L_{\mathrm{bits}}\) binary digits, then
\[
 \operatorname{bits}(d)\le(p+1)^2L_{\mathrm{bits}},
 \qquad \operatorname{bits}(dx)=O(p^2L_{\mathrm{bits}}).
 \tag{18}
\]
This common positive scaling leaves the solution unchanged.  The principal within-view covariance matrix is positive definite by \(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\); hence its leading principal minors, after fixing any ordering of \(A\), are positive and fraction-free elimination needs no pivot.

By \(\texttt{lem:bareiss-minor-growth}\), every division is exact and every transformed coefficient is a signed bordered minor.  If a \(k\times k\) integer matrix \(K\) has entries of magnitude below \(2^h\), the Leibniz formula gives
\[
 |\det K|\le k!2^{kh},
\]
and therefore, using (18) and \(k\le p+1\),
\[
 \operatorname{bits}(\det K)
 =O(p^3L_{\mathrm{bits}}+p\log p).
 \tag{19}
\]
The adjugate identity expresses every regression coordinate as a bordered-minor numerator divided by the nonzero principal determinant.  Greatest-common-divisor reduction with a positive denominator produces a canonical certificate of the height in (19).  Two rational coordinates, rows, or decoded tuples are equal exactly when their canonical certificates agree.

The ordered exact-real algorithm in \(\texttt{thm:exact-once-output-sensitive-enumeration}\) uses polynomially many operations in \(p\), \(m\), \(2^p\), and \(N_{\mathrm{out}}\).  Equations (18)--(19) show that each rational field or comparison operation has polynomial-height operands.  Ordinary integer arithmetic is polynomial in their bit length.  Euclid's algorithm is polynomial as well: after at most two remainder steps its positive second operand is less than half its previous value, so \(h\)-bit inputs require at most \(2h+1\) remainder steps on at most \(h\)-bit operands.  Fragment keys contain \(p\) identifiers of \(O(p)\) bits and create no rational-expression growth.  Published common ancestry is the empty relation by \(\texttt{prop:published-common-union-support-ancestry-empty}\), so its exact output costs \(O(1)\).

Multiplying the polynomial operation count by the polynomial per-operation bit cost, then adding the total emitted encoding length, proves the time assertion.  Multiplying (19) by the stored row and output counts and adding the tries proves the storage assertion.  Each row is solved directly from an original principal covariance system, so the height bound is not recursively iterated through \(2^p\) states.

Stack the views in a fixed order and write \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}=\operatorname{Cov}_P((X^{(a)})_{a\in M})\).  The argument in \(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\) gives \(\Sigma^{aa}\succ0\), so all modified-Cholesky regressions exist.  Fix \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\), and set
\[
 \mathcal L_\pi=\operatorname{diag}_{a\in M}(L_\pi^{(a)}),
 \qquad S_\pi=\mathcal L_\pi\Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}
 \mathcal L_\pi^{\mathsf T}.
 \tag{20}
\]
Each \(L_\pi^{(a)}\) is unit lower triangular after reindexing by \(\pi\), hence invertible, and \(S_\pi\succeq0\).

Let \(e_k^{(a)}\) be the residual from regressing \(X_{\pi(k)}^{(a)}\) on its predecessors \(X_{A_{k-1}}^{(a)}\).  The normal equations give
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_P(e_k^{(a)},X_{\pi(\ell)}^{(a)})=0
 \quad(\ell<k).
 \tag{21}
\]
Every earlier residual is a linear combination of predecessor variables, so (21) makes distinct residuals uncorrelated.  Their variances are the positive Schur complements
\[
 d_{k,a}=\Sigma^{aa}[\pi(k),\pi(k)]-
 \Sigma^{aa}[\pi(k),A_{k-1}]
 \{\Sigma^{aa}[A_{k-1},A_{k-1}]\}^{-1}
 \Sigma^{aa}[A_{k-1},\pi(k)]>0.
 \tag{22}
\]
Thus every within-view block \(S_\pi^{aa}\) is positive diagonal.

Take an orthogonal diagonalization \(S_\pi=U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{mp})U^{\mathsf T}\), with \(\lambda_s\ge0\), and let \(S_\pi^{1/2}=U\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{\lambda_1},\ldots,\sqrt{\lambda_{mp}})U^{\mathsf T}\).  If \(g\) has independent standard normal coordinates, define
\[
 \widetilde\varepsilon=S_\pi^{1/2}g,
 \qquad \widetilde X=\mathcal L_\pi^{-1}\widetilde\varepsilon.
 \tag{23}
\]
Then
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(\widetilde X)
 =\mathcal L_\pi^{-1}S_\pi\mathcal L_\pi^{-\mathsf T}
 =\Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}.
 \tag{24}
\]
Within each view, (21)--(22) make the disturbance covariance positive diagonal.  The Gaussian characteristic function factors as
\[
 \mathbb E\exp\!\left(i\sum_{j\in V}t_j\widetilde\varepsilon_j^{(a)}\right)
 =\exp\!\left(-\tfrac12\sum_{j\in V}d_{j,a}t_j^2\right)
 =\prod_{j\in V}\exp(-d_{j,a}t_j^2/2),
\]
so the within-view coordinates are independent, centered, and nondegenerate.  Equation (23) supplies the structural equations with coefficients \(B_\pi\) and common order \(\pi\).  Thus the witness belongs to \(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{pub}}\), and (24) puts it in \(\mathfrak F_G(\mathcal O_G)\).  This realizes every \(T_\pi\).  All cross-view blocks of \(S_\pi\), including off-diagonal coordinate entries, were retained without restriction.

For the converse, take \((\widetilde P,\widetilde B,\widetilde\varepsilon,\widetilde\pi)\in\mathfrak F_G(\mathcal O_G)\) with \(\widetilde\pi=\pi\).  Fix \(a\), let \(r=\pi(k)\), and set \(A=A_{k-1}\).  Triangularity gives
\[
 \widetilde X_r^{(a)}
 =\widetilde B^{(a)}[r,A]\widetilde X_A^{(a)}
 +\widetilde\varepsilon_r^{(a)},
 \qquad
 \widetilde X_A^{(a)}
 =(I-\widetilde B^{(a)}[A,A])^{-1}
 \widetilde\varepsilon_A^{(a)}.
 \tag{25}
\]
The product disturbance law makes \(\widetilde\varepsilon_r^{(a)}\) independent of \(\widetilde\varepsilon_A^{(a)}\), hence independent of \(\widetilde X_A^{(a)}\).  Centeredness and finite second moments yield zero covariance.  Taking covariance in (25) and using fiber agreement on the marginal block gives
\[
 \Sigma^{aa}[r,A]
 =\widetilde B^{(a)}[r,A]\Sigma^{aa}[A,A].
\]
Positive definiteness permits division, so
\[
 \widetilde B^{(a)}[r,A]
 =\Sigma^{aa}[r,A]\{\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]\}^{-1}
 =B_\pi^{(a)}[r,A].
 \tag{26}
\]
Both rows vanish outside \(A\).  Since \(a\) and \(k\) were arbitrary, \(\widetilde B=B_\pi\).  Taking the order and coefficient projections in \(\texttt{def:compatible-orders}\) and \(\texttt{def:identified-tuple-set}\) proves
\[
 \Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)=\mathfrak S_V,
 \qquad \Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)=\{T_\pi:\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\}.
\]

By \(\texttt{prop:published-common-union-support-ancestry-empty}\), \(\mathcal A_G(\mathcal O_G)=\varnothing\).  This empty relation is exactly the set of ordered pairs that are ancestors in every published-class union-support DAG, by the intersection definition in \(\texttt{def:common-union-support-ancestry}\), and it can be returned in \(O(1)\) time and space.

For completeness, the stream-based procedure asserted in the statement is also valid.  For each \(T=T_\pi\), \(\texttt{def:modified-cholesky}\) places every support edge forward in \(\pi\), so \(\mathcal U(T)\) is a DAG and \(\operatorname{TC}^{+}(\mathcal U(T))\) is its ancestry relation.  Inspecting \(mp^2\) entries, computing reachability in \(O(p^3)\), and intersecting into one \(p\times p\) Boolean accumulator costs \(O(N_{\mathrm{out}}(mp^2+p^3))\) time and \(O(p^2)\) working space.  The stronger constant-time conclusion follows because the result of this intersection is known a priori to be empty.

Every ordering of \(V\setminus A\) is a legal suffix in the full removed-set lattice, so suffix legality depends only on \(A\).  Write a suffix as \((r_1,\ldots,r_{p-|A|})\), set \(A_0=A\), and set \(A_u=A_{u-1}\cup\{r_u\}\).  By \(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\), it appends the immutable rows
\[
 \beta(A_0,r_1),\ \beta(A_1,r_2),\ \ldots,\
 \beta(A_{p-|A|-1},r_{p-|A|}),
 \tag{7}
\]
which depend only on the fixed observed marginals and the displayed predecessor sets.  Thus the same suffix appends the same rows to \(F(\rho)\) and \(F(\rho')\), proving
\[
 F(\rho)=F(\rho')
 \Longrightarrow
 \operatorname{Comp}(\rho)=\operatorname{Comp}(\rho').
 \tag{8}
\]
Every full-lattice prefix has a suffix, so both completion sets are nonempty.  If \(T\) belongs to their intersection, no assigned row is overwritten and \(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\) shows that the projection of \(T\) onto rows in \(A\) is both \(F(\rho)\) and \(F(\rho')\).  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Comp}(\rho)\cap\operatorname{Comp}(\rho')\ne\varnothing
 \Longrightarrow F(\rho)=F(\rho').
 \tag{9}
\]
Equality of the nonempty completion sets implies a nonempty intersection, giving the reverse implication in (8); the contrapositive of (9) gives completion-disjointness.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \((P,B^0,\varepsilon,\Gamma,\pi_0)\in\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) and its observed moments on an arbitrary view graph \(G\).  Then
\[
 \Pi_G^{\mathrm{CA}}(\mathcal O_G)
 =\{\pi\in\mathfrak S_V:\pi\text{ is a source-to-sink path in }
 \mathcal D_G^{\mathrm{live}}\},
\]
and the independently defined coefficient projection satisfies
\[
 \Theta_G^{\mathrm{CA}}(\mathcal O_G)
 =\{T_\pi:\pi\text{ is a source-to-sink path in }
 \mathcal D_G^{\mathrm{live}}\}.
\]
In particular both sets are nonempty.
added_lemmas.proof_tex: The order equality is \(\texttt{thm:qpath-completion-exactness}\), because pruning removes no source-to-sink path.  Let a coefficient family \(\widetilde B\) belong to \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{CA}}(\mathcal O_G)\).  By \(\texttt{def:identified-tuple-set}\), it has a witnessing component-aligned mechanism with some common order \(\pi\).  This witness also belongs to the published fiber.  The converse normal-equation conclusion of \(\texttt{thm:published-all-orders-covariance-compatible}\) gives \(\widetilde B=B_\pi\), and the order equality makes \(\pi\) a source-to-sink path.  Hence the coefficient projection is contained in the displayed path image.  Conversely, for every source-to-sink path, \(\texttt{thm:qpath-completion-exactness}\) constructs a component-aligned Gaussian mechanism matching \(\mathcal O_G\) with coefficient tuple \(T_\pi\), proving the reverse containment.  The generating order \(\pi_0\) itself supplies a fiber member, so the sets are nonempty.

added_lemmas.statement: Fix \((P,B^0,\varepsilon,\Gamma,\pi_0)\in\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) and its observed moments \(\mathcal O_G\), and let \(\rho,\rho'\) be prefixes in \(\mathcal D_G^{\mathrm{live}}\) ending at the same removed set \(A\).  Then \(F(\rho)=F(\rho')\) if and only if \(\operatorname{Comp}_{\mathrm{CA}}(\rho)=\operatorname{Comp}_{\mathrm{CA}}(\rho')\).  Unequal fragments have disjoint nonempty completion sets, and the legal suffix paths depend only on \(A\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex: A legal suffix is a path from \(A\) to \(V\) in the fixed DAG \(\mathcal D_G^{\mathrm{live}}\), so legality depends only on \(A\), not on the prefix.  Source-to-sink pruning makes at least one such suffix available.  If a suffix removes \(r_1,\ldots,r_{p-|A|}\), then \(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\) shows that it appends exactly the rows in (7), independently of the prefix.  Equal fragments therefore have equal completion sets.  If a tuple lies in the intersection of two completion sets, its projection onto the already assigned rows \(A\) equals each prefix fragment, so the fragments are equal.  Nonemptiness turns equality of completion sets into a nonempty intersection, proving the reverse implication; contraposition gives disjointness.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \((P,B^0,\varepsilon,\Gamma,\pi_0)\in\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) and its observed moments \(\mathcal O_G\).  Every fragment in \(H_A^{\mathrm{CA}}\) is the row-\(A\) projection of at least one tuple in \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{CA}}(\mathcal O_G)\).  Distinct fragments at \(A\) have disjoint nonempty output completion sets.  Consequently
\[
 |H_A^{\mathrm{CA}}|\le N_{\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{CA}},
 \qquad
 \sum_{A\subseteq V}|H_A^{\mathrm{CA}}|
 \le2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{CA}},
\]
and at most \(p2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) fragment transitions are attempted.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Induction on \(|A|\) using the component-aligned branch of \(\texttt{def:fragment-hashcons-enumerator}\) gives
\[
 H_A^{\mathrm{CA}}
 =\{F(\rho):\rho\text{ is a prefix in }
 \mathcal D_G^{\mathrm{live}}\text{ ending at }A\}.
\]
For any representing prefix, live pruning supplies a suffix to \(V\), and \(\texttt{thm:component-aligned-fiber-projection-exactness}\) identifies the completed tuple with an element of \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{CA}}(\mathcal O_G)\).  Its row-\(A\) projection is the fragment by \(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\).  Completion sets for unequal fragments are nonempty and disjoint by \(\texttt{lem:component-aligned-live-fragment-right-congruence}\), so charging one distinct output from each set gives \(|H_A^{\mathrm{CA}}|\le N_{\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{CA}}\).  Summing over \(2^p\) subsets and bounding every outdegree by \(p\) gives the remaining inequalities.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \((P,B^0,\varepsilon,\pi_0)\in\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{pub}}\) and its observed moments \(\mathcal O_G\).  Then
\[
 \mathcal A_G(\mathcal O_G)=\varnothing.
\]
Thus unrestricted cross-view pairing contributes no common union-support ancestry, and this published-class output is returned in \(O(1)\) time and space.
added_lemmas.proof_tex: The strict transitive closures in \(\texttt{def:common-union-support-ancestry}\) contain no diagonal pair.  Fix distinct \(i,j\in V\).  Choose a permutation \(\pi\) in which \(j\) precedes \(i\).  By \(\texttt{thm:published-all-orders-covariance-compatible}\), \(T_\pi\in\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\).  Every support edge of \(T_\pi\) points forward in \(\pi\) by \(\texttt{def:modified-cholesky}\); therefore every directed path points forward, and the later vertex \(i\) is not an ancestor of the earlier vertex \(j\).  Thus \((i,j)\notin\operatorname{TC}^{+}(\mathcal U(T_\pi))\), so it is absent from the intersection defining \(\mathcal A_G(\mathcal O_G)\).  This excludes every ordered pair and proves emptiness.  Returning the predeclared empty relation takes constant time and space.

added_lemmas.statement: Fix \((P,B^0,\varepsilon,\Gamma,\pi_0)\in\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) and its observed moments \(\mathcal O_G\).  Then \(\mathcal A_G^{\mathrm{CA}}(\mathcal O_G)\) is exactly the set of ordered pairs that are ancestors in the union-support DAG of every mechanism in \(\mathfrak F_G^{\mathrm{CA}}(\mathcal O_G)\).  Given the exact-once component-aligned tuple stream, it is computed by exact support tests, transitive closure, and intersection in \(O(N_{\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{CA}}(mp^2+p^3))\) additional time and \(O(p^2)\) working space.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \((P,B^0,\varepsilon,\Gamma,\pi_0)\in\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) and observed moments \(\mathcal O_G\) on an arbitrary view graph \(G\). \[

 +p^3 2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{CA}}
 +mp^2N_{\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{CA}}\right),
\]
and its time and space are \(O(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p\max\{1,N_{\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{CA}}\})\).  It uses deterministic exact row interning and integer tries, not a real hash oracle or an enumeration of all \(p!\) orders.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Induction on subset size proves that \(H_A^{\mathrm{CA}}\) is exactly the set of distinct fragments of prefixes in \(\mathcal D_G^{\mathrm{live}}\) ending at \(A\).  The induction step follows every live edge and writes its immutable row; merging is safe and complete by \(\texttt{lem:component-aligned-live-fragment-right-congruence}\).  At \(V\), fragments are full tuples, and \(\texttt{thm:component-aligned-fiber-projection-exactness}\) gives
\[
 \{\text{decoded members of }H_V^{\mathrm{CA}}\}
 =\Theta_G^{\mathrm{CA}}(\mathcal O_G).
\]
Exact lexicographic row interning identifies precisely equal numerical rows, and a deterministic binary trie retains precisely one copy of each integer fragment.  This proves exact-once output.

For preprocessing, compute each within-view Schur state and each observed cross-view Schur state directly from \(\mathcal O_G\).  For a fixed subset, dense factorizations and matrix products cost \(O((m+|E|)p^3)\); over all subsets this is \(O((m+|E|)p^3 2^p)\).  The \(q\)-tests cost \(O(|E|p^2 2^p)\), and constructing and pruning the at most \(p2^{p-1}\) edges costs \(O(p2^p)\), both absorbed.  Computing all immutable rows and sorting them by original row label costs \(O(mp^3 2^p)\), also absorbed.

Each integer-fragment trie operation costs \(O(p^2)\).  By \(\texttt{lem:component-aligned-projection-output-bound}\), at most \(p2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) transitions are attempted, giving \(O(p^3 2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{CA}})\) propagation time. State covariances and interned rows occupy \(O((m+|E|)p^2 2^p)\) exact-real cells.  The fragment tries occupy \(O(p^2 2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{CA}})\) bits or pointers by the projection bound, outputs occupy \(O(mp^2N_{\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{CA}})\) cells, and the ancestry accumulator occupies \(O(p^2)\) bits. added_lemmas.statement: Under the premises of \(\texttt{thm:component-aligned-exact-once-output-sensitive-enumeration}\), suppose every entry of the rational input \(\mathcal O_G\) has binary encoding length at most \(L_{\mathrm{bits}}\). added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Apply the denominator clearing and Bareiss argument of \(\texttt{thm:rational-output-polynomial-bit-enumeration}\) to every principal within-view solve. Each score \(q^{ab}(A,r,t)\) divides only by \(C_A^{bb}[r,r]>0\), as proved in \(\texttt{thm:qpath-completion-exactness}\), and exact zero is decided by cross multiplication of polynomial-height integers.

Canonical row certificates, integer fragment keys, exact support tests, Boolean transitive closure, and all rational arithmetic therefore have polynomial bit cost per operation and polynomial stored height. prose_updates.tldr: The observed covariance law supports two exact but different conclusions. Under the published shared-order LiMVAM primitives, unrestricted cross-view disturbance dependence makes every order covariance-compatible and makes common union-support ancestry empty, so pairing contributes neither pruning nor ancestry. Under the component-aligned subclass, the independently defined mechanism fiber is exactly represented by source-to-sink paths of the live \(q\)-DAG. A two-mode immutable-row dynamic program emits each distinct coefficient tuple once; its pairing-informative component-aligned mode runs in \(O((m+|E|)p^3 2^p+p^3 2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{CA}}+mp^2N_{\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{CA}})\) ordered exact-real time and computes the nontrivial subclass ancestry intersection, with a corresponding rational output-polynomial guarantee.

project_justification.fill: Source-to-sink pruning makes every retained prefix extendable. sampling_model.design: The population input is the exact collection of within-view covariance blocks and cross-view blocks observed on an arbitrary fixed graph \(G\). The published mode uses only marginal regressions because edge residuals are unrestricted nuisance. The component-aligned mode additionally computes edgewise Schur states and \(q\)-scores, constructs the full \(2^p\) compatibility DAG, and prunes it from source to sink.
sampling_model.units: Within each covariance source, observations are independent and identically distributed from the corresponding marginal of one target law \(P\). Different sources need not be independent because units may be reused.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment. The structural targets are the coefficient projections of the published and component-aligned mechanism fibers and the ancestry relations common to their union-support DAGs.
sampling_model.overlap: Only edges of \(G\) require paired measurements. The published layer assumes centered finite-second-moment product disturbances within each view, positive within-view variances, and a shared order, while allowing arbitrary cross-view disturbance covariance. The pairing-informative layer additionally assumes cross-coordinate component alignment and positive-definite coordinate-stack covariance.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: All new results are exact population identification and enumeration statements. Sampling uncertainty is inherited only through the parent's covariance-region inversion; no new estimator rate, limit law, polynomial enumeration of a continuum region, or substitution of a point enumerator for region inversion is claimed.

prose_updates.interpretation: Unrestricted cross-view pairing is causally uninformative at the covariance level in this model: every order has a Gaussian covariance witness, and choosing the reverse order for any pair proves that published common ancestry is empty. Component alignment changes the conclusion. Its observed edge blocks prune the order set through the live \(q\)-DAG, and the exact-once stream yields a potentially nonempty common ancestry intersection. Numerical fragment merging can be substantial in both modes because many structural orders may induce the same coefficient tuple.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The guarantees are total output-sensitive bounds over an explicit \(2^p\) state space, not polynomial delay and not polynomial time in \(p\). Ordered exact-real arithmetic is not a floating-point stability guarantee; the rational theorem controls bit complexity only. The \(q\)-DAG theorem requires maintained component-aligned inputs and does not provide polynomial preprocessing for arbitrary off-model nonchordal partial covariances. Gaussianity is used only to construct existential completion witnesses, not assumed of the generating law. The results enumerate exact population coefficient sets, not continuum-valued covariance-region inverses.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The published shared-order class retains arbitrary cross-view disturbance covariance: pairing supplies neither order pruning nor common ancestry there, although the full-lattice algorithm still removes numerical duplicates without enumerating permutations. The pairing-informative result is exactly the component-aligned subclass with positive-definite coordinate covariance blocks, on an arbitrary observed view graph and at model-generated population moments. It proves q-path/fiber equivalence, exact-once tuple enumeration, nontrivial ancestry post-processing, ordered-exact-real complexity, and rational output-polynomial complexity. It does not claim unrestricted LiMVAM identification, polynomial delay, off-model nonchordal completion, floating-point robustness, or finite enumeration of the parent's covariance-region inverse.
